guitar.notes: Corrected: Kim Thayil is Soundgarden's guitarist; Chris Cornell was primarily vocalist (occasionally rhythm guitar) so listing him as co-equal guitarist overstates his role. Kim Thayil's Guild S-100 is reasonably well documented.

tone.target: thick fuzzed grunge crunch with wah bite
tone.profile: thick fuzzed grunge crunch with wah bite
tone.summary: Fuzz -> Wah -> Boost/OD -> High Gain Amp (UK 800) -> Cab (4x12) -> EQ -> Chorus/Delay for depth.
corrections: replace generic grunge with fuzzed riff tone

rig.name: Soundgarden - Jesus Christ Pose - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Achieve the thick Big Muff style fuzz foundation.
Provide the decisive wah bite required for the riffing.
Add aggressive sustain and push the fuzz into the amp.
blocks.gap: Using Boost for general drive lift, as a dedicated OD might clash with the heavy fuzz.

blocks.purpose: Simulate the Marshall-ish high gain and thick British crunch.
Provide the classic 4x12 cabinet tone for grunge rock.
Boost the low end and dirty mids to prevent scooping.
Add subtle depth and width to the thick fuzz tone.
blocks.gap: Chorus is used sparingly here; a simpler delay might also work, but Chorus adds necessary texture.

blocks.purpose: Add rhythmic echo and space to the aggressive riffs.
blocks.gap: A simple delay is needed to give the heavy tone some dimension without sounding muddy.

improvements.summary: Improve cabinet realism to better capture the thick, aggressive grunge tone.

proposals.reason: Enhance grit and thickness for grunge rock.
